extracted.intended_audience: patent lawyers, judges, law students, and other practitioners in U.S. patent law
extracted.subtask_description: A table-of-contents style listing of topics, standards, and procedural rules in U.S. patent law (infringement, jurisdiction, pleadings, defences, damages, injunctions, profits, and statutory provisions). Useful as an organizational rubric for legal analysis and practice in patent litigation and prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doctrine of equivalents / necessity of equivalence
rubrics_metrics.description: Question of the necessity of ... in equivalents (treatment of equivalence issues in infringement analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses when and to what extent a device or process not literally within the claims may nonetheless infringe under the doctrine of equivalents; surrounding text in the book treats primary/secondary inventions and review sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary and secondary inventions re: doctrine of equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary and secondary inventions in respect of the doctrine of equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes between primary and secondary inventions when applying the doctrine of equivalents (scope and limitations of equivalence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evasion by changes of form
rubrics_metrics.description: Evasion of the patent by changes of form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers whether infringers can avoid liability by altering form/shape while practicing the claimed invention; linked to equivalence and infringement tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes of form in infringement questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of form considered in respect of questions of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of when a change of form is material to infringement or merely a non-substantive alteration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature of use and infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Nature of use considered in respect of questions of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers how the way an accused device/process is used affects infringement analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement of patents for compositions of matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringement of patents for compositions of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines particular issues arising in composition cases (ingredients, proportions, substitutions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitution of ingredients
rubrics_metrics.description: Substitution of ingredients (including equivalents and non-equivalents).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When substitution of an ingredient in a composition constitutes infringement; includes notion of equivalent vs non-equivalent ingredients and illustrative case law (e.g., Giant-Powder cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclaimers of particular equivalents
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclaimers of particular equivalents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How explicit disclaimers in the patent or prosecution history limit the scope of equivalents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes of proportion in compositions
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of proportion in compositions of matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether and when changes in relative proportions of ingredients avoid or incur infringement liability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringement of design patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Infringements of patents for designs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles and tests specific to design-patent infringement (distinct from utility patents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative utility as a criterion of infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Comparative utility as a criterion of infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of comparative utility (whether the accused article performs essentially the same function/use) in determining infringement; applicability varies by context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of the patent not required for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge of a patent by an infringer is not a necessary element in its infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement is a strict-liability inquiry in many contexts; intent/knowledge may matter for damages (e.g., willfulness) but not for liability per se.

rubrics_metrics.name: Federal courts' jurisdiction in patent cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of United States courts of first resort in patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets out which federal courts have original jurisdiction over patent disputes and the statutory/constitutional bases for jurisdiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: State courts' jurisdiction limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-jurisdiction of State courts in patent cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains limits on state-court jurisdiction over patent causes of action and exceptions/qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-court jurisdiction over contract controversies relevant to patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of State courts over controversies growing out of contracts relevant to patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes pure patent suits from contract disputes that may be litigated in state court when only contract issues (not patent validity) are raised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction of individual federal courts and the Court of Claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of individual United States courts of first resort in patent cases; jurisdiction of the Court of Claims and limits concerning unauthorized making/using/selling by the United States Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains allocation of venue and special rules where the government or its agents are involved; covers absence/presence of jurisdiction in particular contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be plaintiff / complainant in a patent action
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may be a plaintiff or complainant in a patent action, including issues about assignees, executors, administrators, licensees, owners-in-common, and nominal plaintiffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules on standing, assignment of accrued claims, who may sue in their own name, and limitations on nominal plaintiffs (e.g., licensees cannot be purely nominal plaintiffs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may be made a defendant in patent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Who may be made a defendant in a patent action: minors, married women, agents, salesmen, employers, persons causing others to infringe, joint infringers, contributory infringers, partners, corporations, officers, directors, shareholders, consolidated corporations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories of potential defendants and special rules for corporate officers/stockholders and consolidated entities; includes contributory infringement notions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory liability of officers, directors, stockholders
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory liability of officers, directors, and stockholders of corporations in patent litigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When corporate agents or owners may be held personally liable under statutes or common law doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causes of action involving multiple IP rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Causes of action based on a plurality of patents or on both terms of an extended patent, or on a patent and a trade-mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How claims may be pleaded and litigated when multiple patents or mixed intellectual-property rights are involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forms of actions for infringement; fraud in procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of actions for infringement; actions for fraudulently procuring a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appropriate forms of pleading, and when an action for fraud in procurement is available as a cause separate from ordinary infringement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleading the right of action and substantive allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Declarations and statements of the right of action covering novelty, utility, prior public use/sale (statutory bars), identity of the patentee vs inventor, application, letters patent, reissue, disclaimer, extension, plaintiff's title, profert of title, marking 'patented', infringement, time of infringement, damages, and conclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the substantive items that must (or typically should) be alleged in a declaration for infringement and related procedural particulars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial (not merely technical) accuracy required in declarations
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial and not technical accuracy required in declarations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleading standard: plaintiffs must plead the case with substantial accuracy rather than hyper-technical exactness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dilatory pleas and a catalog of bar defences
rubrics_metrics.description: Dilatory pleas and twenty-eight defences pleadable in bar in patent actions (including estoppel, statutes of limitations, laches, prior adjudication, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates recognized defences and procedural posture for asserting them; specific defenses (estoppel, statute of limitations, etc.) are treated in detail in following sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Estoppel doctrines (res judicata, by deed, pleading rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estoppel by matter of record: res judicata; estoppel by matter of deed; how the twenty-sixth defence (estoppel) is pleaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains different estoppel mechanisms and pleading/charge requirements in patent litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutes of limitations as defence
rubrics_metrics.description: The twenty-seventh defence; statutes of limitations and national vs state statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses the applicable limitation periods (national statute of limitation vs state statutes) and their interplay with patent causes of action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural devices: replications, demurrers, joinders
rubrics_metrics.description: Replications, rejoinders, sur-rejoinders, demurrers to declarations and pleas, joinders in demurrer, notices of special matter, and other special pleading topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers pleading practice in patent cases and treatment of special matters that need not be pleaded (judicial notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial procedures in patent actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial of actions at law for infringement of patents, including trial by jury, rules of practice, rules of evidence, and how letters patent and reissue patents are used as evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers general trial mechanics and evidentiary rules specific to patent litigation (admission of letters patent, presumptions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters patent as evidence and presumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters patent as evidence; reissue letters patent as evidence; letters patent presumed to be in force until end of term on their face.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effect and evidentiary weight given to patents and reissues in litigation; presumptions as to validity/term may apply subject to rebuttal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of title and marking requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of title; marking 'patented' and pleading/proof related to marking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof necessary to show title and effects/penalties of marking or false marking; marking issues affect notice and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of expert evidence in patent trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert evidence of infringement; hypothetical questions for experts; expert testimony relevant to the state of the art; cross-examination of experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for admissibility and framing of expert testimony; how experts are used to establish infringement, technical state of the art, and damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence to sustain specific defences
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence rules and types required to sustain particular defences (various numbered defences described later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizes the types of proof a defendant must present to support different affirmative or negative defences (prior use, prior patents, prior publications, license, estoppel, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: When judge may direct verdict for defendant; jury instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: When the judge may direct the jury to return a verdict for the defendant; instructions to juries; verdicts; new trials; trials by judge without jury; trial by referee; judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for directed verdicts, jury charge, and post-trial relief in patent trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs, fees, and taxation of costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs, including attorney's docket fees, clerk's fees, magistrate's fees, witness fees, taxation of costs, and statutory rules governing costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Which costs are recoverable in patent litigation and procedural rules for taxation of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic measure of damages and royalty concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic measure of damages; established royalties as specific measures of damages; tests applied to royalties on behalf of defendants and plaintiffs; reasonable royalties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frameworks for computing damages: established royalties, reasonable royalties, and tests courts apply when determining appropriate royalty rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Money paid for past infringement not a measure of damages in another case
rubrics_metrics.description: Money paid for infringement already committed is no measure of damages in another case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past settlements/royalties are not automatically determinative of damages in separate litigation, though they may be evidence in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Royalties on sales and licenses; proportion of licensed to unlicensed practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Royalties reserved on sales of patents; royalties for licenses to make and use vs to make and sell; proportion of licensed to unlicensed practice of an invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How royalties are allocated and considered in damages, including differences between license types and market practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurtful competition and recoverable damages absent established royalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurtful competition in the absence of an established royalty causes recoverable damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no established royalty exists, courts may assess damages based on competitive harm and other equitable factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages for unlicensed making without unlicensed selling or using
rubrics_metrics.description: Damages for unlicensed making, without unlicensed selling or using.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treatment of cases where manufacture alone (without sale/use) occurs — what damages are recoverable and how measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of damages and indirect/consequential damages
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence of damages; indirect consequential damages; reasonable royalties; exemplary and increased damages; actual damages not affected by infringement being unintended; counsel fees and other expenses; interest on damages; damages in design cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed rules and evidentiary standards for awarding different categories of damages, punitive/treble awards, fee awards, and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equity jurisdiction in patent causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction of equity in patent causes; jurisdiction of equity to assess and decree damages; equity's jurisdiction over infringing articles before and after decree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When equitable relief (injunction, accounting, equitable damages) is proper alongside or instead of legal remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parts of an equity bill and practice in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The complainant; the defendant; original bills; title of the court; introductory part; stating part; prayer for relief; interrogating part; prayer for process; signature; oaths to bills; amendments to bills when allowed/necessary; demurrers, pleas and answers in equity; pleas and replications; particulars of claim and defence; interrogatories and what interrogatories are proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural composition and practice for equitable pleadings in patent suits (how to draft and respond to bills in equity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences in equity; laches; prior adjudication; conspiracy defence
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences in equity including laches (how set up), prior adjudication at law, laches-related defences, conspiracy by plaintiff in restraint of trade as a defence, counterclaims and set-offs in answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equitable defences that can bar or mitigate relief in patent equity suits and how they should be pleaded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental bills, bills of revivor, and interlocutory practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplemental bills; bills in nature of supplemental bills; bills of revivor; leave of court to file supplemental bills; demurrers/pleas/answers to supplemental bills; interlocutory hearings; questions of law and fact on hearings; evidence in support of bill and defences; depositions; documentary evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural mechanisms to continue or modify equity proceedings and associated evidentiary practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and practice on interlocutory appeals, rehearings, and final decrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Interlocutory decrees; appeals from interlocutory decrees; petitions for rehearings (on matters apparent on record and newly discovered evidence); final decrees; bills of review; appeals; hearings on appeals; decisions on appeals; certificates of division of opinion; writs of certiorari; costs on appeals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellate practice and post-decree remedies in patent equity litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injunctions: jurisdiction, forms, preliminary and temporary relief
rubrics_metrics.description: Jurisdiction to grant injunctions; form of injunctions; preliminary injunctions; bills and notices of motions for preliminary injunctions; motions for and suspensions of preliminary injunctions; temporary restraining orders; elements of prima facie rights to preliminary injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards for preliminary equitable relief in patent cases (what must be shown for preliminary injunctions and TROs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public acquiescence and prior adjudication as bar to injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior adjudication; public acquiescence (duration and effect) as factors averting preliminary injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How prior rulings or extended public acquiescence in practice can defeat a patent owner's request for equitable relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defences to motions for preliminary injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defences to motions for preliminary injunctions by traverse or confession and avoidance; averting effect of prior adjudication/public acquiescence; proving repeal/expiration of patent or fault in title; proving license; proving estoppel; showing laches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates common tactical and substantive defences to preliminary injunctive relief and the types of proof required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonds, discretion, dissolution, and consequences of injunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Bonds instead of injunctions; bonds required from complainants in certain cases; discretion of the court in granting/refusing injunctions; motions to dissolve preliminary injunctions (for errors of law or newly discovered evidence); reinstatement of dissolved injunctions; consequences of obedience/disobedience to injunctions subsequently dissolved; appeals from preliminary injunctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural and equitable considerations affecting issuance, dissolution, and enforcement of injunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent injunctions: scope, refusal grounds, duration, territorial scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Permanent injunctions; refusal because patent expired, assigned, defendant dead/dissolved; cessation of infringement not ground for refusal; not refused because of non-use; postponement/suspension pending appeals; dissolution; duration limited by term of patent; territorial scope of injunctions; penalties for violations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When permanent injunctive relief is appropriate and its limits (term-limited, territorial reach, special circumstances that bar or modify relief).

rubrics_metrics.name: Infringer's profits and accounting in equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The infringer's profits recoverable in equity: joint infringement, partly unprofitable infringements, time spans covered, generic rule for ascertaining profits, complainant's damages not criterion for defendant's profits, defendant's profits when unlawfully making/selling, ascertainment of cost of making/selling infringing articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standards and methods for awarding an accounting of profits and how profits are separated from other sources of gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof and methods to separate profits due to patented features
rubrics_metrics.description: Burden of proof when it is necessary to separate profits due to patented features from profits due to other features; methods where defendant made and sold the patented invention separately or in combination; selection of proper standard of comparison; credits due to defendant's improvements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How courts allocate burdens and choose methods (comparative cost, separate accounting, apportionment) to identify profits attributable to the patented invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where no separation is required and comparative cost criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases where no separation is required or allowed; method of making the separation by the criterion of comparative cost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Circumstances where courts award all profits vs require apportionment, and the comparative-cost approach to apportionment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affirmative gain vs saving from loss; interest on profits
rubrics_metrics.description: Affirmative gain; saving from loss; affirmative gain and saving from loss; interest on infringer's profits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes profit concepts and whether interest may be awarded on recovered profits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings before masters and master's reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before masters; evidence before masters; objections to evidence before masters; master's reports; exceptions to master's report; defendants' affirmative/negative exceptions; complainants' exceptions; outline of practice relevant to master's findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice and deference given to masters in complex accounting and fact-finding tasks in equity suits for profits/damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent statutes: administrative and substantive provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Appendix listing many patent statutes and statutory sections: establishment of Patent Office; officers and employees; printing of specifications and drawings; requisites of specification and claim; what inventions are patentable; drawings; specimens; model; oath; examination and issuing patents; limitation on time to complete application; patents to assignees; renewal for failure to pay fees; assignment; marking requirements and penalties for false marking; filing/effect of caveats; notice of rejection of claim; interferences; affidavits, depositions, subpoenas, witness fees; appeals from examiners; reissue; disclaimer; suits for infringement; power of courts to grant injunctions; extensions; fees and mode of payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Catalog of statutory authorities and procedural/administrative rules that govern patent procurement, maintenance, enforcement, and remedies; each referenced section corresponds to a statutory topic discussed in the treatise.
